how: generated cells, copied whole — 18 of the 210 of `scripts/silent-sweep/d199/gen199.py`, kept WHOLE (all three `fld` legs and both `order` legs) because a refused candidate's price is not collapsible. Same regenerate/materialise commands as d199-rungs.json.
note: THE REFUSED CANDIDATE AND ITS PRICE (silent-class-inventory D351). When this set was filed, 12 of these were `trap_loads` on the shipped tree and 6 `run`. The obvious extension of D199 — fold a union arm's `$fnsig` slot onto the DECLARED STRUCT row whose heap type D280 already merged it with — was BUILT and graded: it buys all 12 and costs the 6, `runs` -> check-clean invalid wasm, because the token CHAR is what `sigParamKindAt` reports. A cell falling into silence is not a trade this family takes, and the set was kept whole so nobody paid that price again without noticing. #1994 then closed D351 somewhere else entirely — `cloSigTwin`, a fold of two POOL entries whose functypes render byte-identically, which leaves every KEY untouched — and the same 12 go to `runs` while the 6 do not move at all. So all 18 now RUN, the 12 as tripwires for the close and the 6 as the standing price of the producer-level fold.
ablation: on `4a6c1e52` and on `7d3698a4`: 12 trap_loads + 6 runs. Under the cross-fold candidate: 18 runs, of which 6 are check-clean invalid wasm counted as runs LOST. Under #1994's pool fold: 18 runs, 0 lost, and the 6 are byte-identical to what they were. Neither half is derivable from current behaviour — the 12 look like their running neighbours to every collapse that does not know what a candidate did to them, and the 6 look like ordinary value calls.

d199_hofcross_decl_i32_norm.why: D351's population, CLOSED by #1994 and kept as a tripwire: an inline lambda minted under the DECLARED STRUCT twin's spelling handed to the ARM's callee. It was `trap_loads` when the set was filed — one `uVarHeap` heap type (D280's cross-table merge) under TWO `$fnsig` keys, `V…;` and `s…;`, and two identical functypes at two indices of one rec group are DISTINCT types in WasmGC. The pool's byte-identity fold (`cloSigTwin`) makes the two keys name ONE type index; a compiler that traps here again has lost that fold.

d199_vcall_narrow_decl_i32_norm.why: THE PRICE, and it is why D351 stays open. Folding the arm's `$fnsig` token onto the struct twin's (`repSigSlotTokOfKind("struct", variantStructHeapTwinAt(rep))`) buys the 12 cells above and takes these 6 from `runs` to check-clean invalid wasm: the token CHAR is what `sigParamKindAt` reports, so an arm parameter spelled `s…;` stops being a `variant` parameter and the value-call arm coercion never fires on it.
